key_insight: SLoSa combines symbolic verification with model compression and fine-tuning to build compact, safety-aware language-model planners for robots.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports local robotic task planning under resource constraints, with INT4 models averaging 17.85–26.41 W on Jetson Orin.
method: Build safety-aware training data using classical planners, a teacher LLM, and formal verifiers.
Apply supervised fine-tuning to compact foundation models.
Use reinforcement learning with a verification-based reward machine for safety alignment.
evidence_signal: Evaluation spans four PDDL domains, two household simulators, edge platforms, and a robotic arm; verifier-guided post-training yields 70.5–76.0% success for 4B–14B planners on PDDL tasks.
watch_item: Safety alignment depends on the encoded constraints and verifier coverage; reported task success does not establish universal real-world safety.
paper_title: SLoSa: Small, Low-Power, and Safe Foundation Models for Robotic Task Planning
